cards.explanation: The answer is his relatives and close friends. Verse 24 says Cornelius, the Roman centurion (Acts 10:1), had called together his relatives and close friends. I think that's a man too excited to keep good news to himself. Friends, if my family lived nearby I'd have called them too, and then I'd have lit the oven.

The answer is False. Peter helped Cornelius up. He told him, "Stand up… I am only a man myself." (Acts 10:26) If somebody dropped down in front of me, I'd say the same thing, friends. I'm just a stamper with a big mustache.

The answer is False. Peter says it's unlawful for a Jew to associate with a foreigner or visit him. Then he adds, "But God has shown me that I should not call any man impure or unclean." (Acts 10:28) He names the rule, and then he says what God showed him.

The answer is without objection. Peter says, "So when I was invited, I came without objection." (Acts 10:29) He just says it and shows up. Friends, I've seen grown men argue with a snooze button longer than that.

The answer is that his prayer was heard and his gifts remembered. The man in radiant clothing says, "Cornelius, your prayer has been heard, and your gifts to the poor have been remembered before God." (Acts 10:31) Both are named in that one sentence, prayer first and gifts second. Both are said to be before God.

The answer is True. The man in radiant clothing said it plainly. He tells Cornelius that Peter "…is a guest in the home of Simon the tanner, by the sea." (Acts 10:32) He gives Cornelius the name and the place. That's about as clear as directions get.

The answer is to listen to everything the Lord told Peter to say. Cornelius says, "Now then, we are all here in the presence of God to listen to everything the Lord has instructed you to tell us." (Acts 10:33) The whole room is ready to listen. I wish every audience came that ready, friends.

The answer is that God does not show favoritism. Peter says, "I now truly understand that God does not show favoritism…" (Acts 10:34) The word "now" matters there. He's standing in a Gentile's house when he says it. I think that's a man who just learned something big and said it right away.

The answer is True. Peter says God "…welcomes those from every nation who fear Him and do what is right." (Acts 10:35) Every nation is in that sentence, friends. And Peter says it with a room of Gentiles right in front of him.

The answer is Lord of all. Peter says Jesus Christ "…is Lord of all." (Acts 10:36) He says it right after mentioning the message sent to the people of Israel. And he's saying it in a house full of Gentiles.

The answer is doing good and healing the oppressed. Peter says Jesus "…went around doing good and healing all who were oppressed by the devil…" (Acts 10:38) Doing good and healing, again and again, all the way around. That's the picture Peter paints, friends.

The answer is that God was with Him. Peter says Jesus went around doing good and healing all who were oppressed by the devil, "…because God was with Him." (Acts 10:38) That's the reason he gives for the doing good and the healing. He names God being with Him, and no other reason.
The answer is third. Peter says, "God raised Him up on the third day…" (Acts 10:40) Just that, and nothing about how it happened. Three is the number he gives, friends.

The answer is witnesses God had chosen beforehand. Peter says it was "…not by all the people, but by the witnesses God had chosen beforehand…" (Acts 10:41) God did the choosing, and He did it beforehand. Peter counts himself among them with the word "us."
The answer is False. These witnesses were close, friends. Peter says they were "…us who ate and drank with Him after He rose from the dead." (Acts 10:41) That's a table, not a telescope.

The answer is the living and the dead. Peter says Jesus "…is the One appointed by God to judge the living and the dead." (Acts 10:42) God appointed Him, and Peter names both the living and the dead. He is also the Lord of all, as Peter said in verse 36.

The answer is everyone who believes in Him. Peter says, "…everyone who believes in Him receives forgiveness of sins through His name." (Acts 10:43) Everyone who believes, and it's through His name. Peter says it right after saying that all the prophets testify about Him.

The answer is that the Holy Spirit falls on all who heard. Verse 44 says that while Peter was still speaking these words, "…the Holy Spirit fell upon all who heard his message." Not some of them, all who heard. The timing is right there in the verse: Peter was still speaking.

The answer is that the Spirit was poured out even on the Gentiles. The text says the circumcised believers were astounded "…that the gift of the Holy Spirit had been poured out even on the Gentiles." (Acts 10:45) Gentiles are people who aren't Jews. I think the word "even" says a lot, because the gift reached people they weren't expecting it to reach.
The answer is God. Verse 46 says they heard them "…speaking in tongues and exalting God." The words they spoke lifted God up, friends. That's the sound that filled the house.
The answer is False. Peter says, "They have received the Holy Spirit just as we have!" (Acts 10:47) He's pointing at what he just saw. Same Spirit, same gift.

The answer is Jesus Christ. Verse 48 says Peter "…ordered that they be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ." Earlier in the sermon he'd said that everyone who believes in Jesus receives forgiveness of sins through His name (Acts 10:43). His name is the name that matters here, friends.

The answer is True. The text says, "Then they asked him to stay for a few days." (Acts 10:48) The verse tells us they asked, and it names a few days. I think that's a house that wasn't ready for the visit to end. And the story isn't over, friends.
